## Natural history notes

A slender assassin bug characterized by an elongated orange to reddish-brown body, long legs and antennae, and a narrow head with a piercing beak tucked beneath it. In Florida, Doldina interjungens is recorded from the state, including South Florida, and is most likely found in warm open or semi-open habitats such as scrubby edges, gardens, pine flatwoods, hammocks, and areas where insect prey is common. It is a predatory true bug, using its beak to stab and feed on other small insects and arthropods, and like other assassin bugs it should be observed without handling because it can deliver a painful defensive bite.
